identity: Astronomer and university teacher · United Kingdom · 1900–1979
title: Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin's birth chart
metaDescription: Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.4° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds an opposition to Saturn at 0.2° — close enough to weld taste to structure. The scheme reads an opposition as an axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 19.4° into Taurus — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 29.1° Aries, Venus at 4.3° Cancer, Mars at 24.8° Aries. Mercury in a fire sign reads as thought that arrives already in motion; Venus in a water sign reads as attraction that works by atmosphere; Mars in a fire sign reads as effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Venus and Saturn: 0.2° from an exact opposition. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Mars sextile Neptune at 0.5°, and Jupiter conjunction Uranus at 3.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, three placements stand out. Mars in Aries at 24.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 8.1° is in domicile; Saturn in Capricorn at 4.5° is in domicile. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 fire, 2 earth, 2 air, 1 water by element and 4 cardinal, 4 mutable, 1 fixed by mode. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.0° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
